question: Can native VAE/Klein spatial features distinguish known fine-geometry failure from substantially successful geometry without merely ranking global appearance change?
saved_artifact_policy: Use Phase 2 decoded x0 previews. No diffusion trajectory is rerun. Re-encode saved previews because exact latent/hidden tensors were not persisted.
representations: Klein midpoint after single_block_7 generated slice [B,1024,3072]
conditioning_policy: For each source/current pair, use the same case transformation conditioning and the saved evaluation sigma. This prevents prompt choice from differing between paired features.

correspondence.metric: cosine nearest neighbor in a clipped 9x9 window around each source token
correspondence.confidence: best cosine minus second-best cosine, plus best cosine
correspondence.displacement: Euclidean token displacement from source coordinate to best current coordinate
correspondence.local_distance: one minus cosine at the unchanged coordinate
correspondence.weighted_distribution: weight displacement by normalized source spatial gradient magnitude
correspondence.regions: top gradient quartile is structure-bearing source-region proxy; bottom gradient quartile is background proxy

selection_rule: A useful signal must rank both portrait arms as more drifted than the four successful astronaut/bridge arms at final evaluation, with trajectory behavior and confidence supporting the separation. No layer or radius tuning after results.
